items.headline: adidas Tokyo goes full ballerina
items.caption: Taipei label Fruition turns the slim adidas Tokyo into a luxe ballet sneaker.
body: Fruition's Tokyo Ballerina uses top suede, stitched leather stripes and quilted insoles.
Sheer ribbons replace laces, and the scrunched upper gives a real ballet-shoe feel.
How to wear it: cropped wide trousers so the ribbons show.

items.headline: Is the luxury fleece era over?
items.caption: A$AP Rocky keeps wearing a $148 Alo half-zip instead of designer fleece.
body: Rocky stepped out again in Alo, the LA athleisure brand better known for leggings.
Highsnobiety reads it as a sign that very expensive look-alike designer fleece is losing its pull.
How to wear it: a plain half-zip over a tee, with straight-leg trousers.

items.headline: Nike squares off the Air Force 1
items.caption: The 'Squair Toe' AF1 Low lands in black and white textured leather.
body: It keeps the classic perforations and Air sole but slims and squares the toe box.
Premium textured leather leans into a dressier, almost formal look.
How to wear it: with tailored trousers where you'd normally wear loafers.

items.headline: Nike's P-6000 dresses in 'Thunder Blue'
items.caption: Cordura that looks like denim gives the dad sneaker a workwear edge.
body: It isn't denim but Cordura, a tough nylon-like fabric used in workwear and army uniforms.
It's the first Cordura P-6000 in a while, and Highsnobiety calls these the best versions.
How to wear it: carpenter trousers and a chore jacket.

items.headline: Frank Ocean's new Prada sneaker
items.caption: A rare Instagram Story shows Frank in Prada's updated America's Cup.
body: The shoe updates Prada's 1997 sailing sneaker made for the Luna Rossa team.
The new one uses brushed leather and bike fabric and is lighter and sleeker.
How to wear it: a crisp white shirt and relaxed navy trousers.

items.headline: New Balance 990v7 breaks the dad-shoe mold
items.caption: Only the seventh version of New Balance's flagship since 1982.
body: New Balance rarely updates the 990; the last version was the v6 in 2022.
GQ says the v7 might be the best one yet.
How to wear it: grey 990s, grey sweats, navy overcoat. Classic.

items.headline: The liner: a jacket for your jacket
items.caption: Highsnobiety's picks of quilted liner jackets and vests for the cold snap.
body: A liner is a light, usually quilted layer you wear under your outerwear.
It's for days when a rain jacket isn't enough and a puffer is too much.
How to wear it: an olive quilted vest under an open mac.

items.headline: Eckhaus Latta moves to the Lower East Side
items.caption: The label's new Ludlow Street shop is built to be a hangout.
body: Eckhaus Latta has left its tiny Chinatown Mall store for the heart of the Lower East Side.
'We've graduated from the Chinatown Mall,' the brand's press manager says.
The space keeps the neighbourhood's scrappy charm, graffiti included.

items.headline: Monad at 10: still refusing to scale up
items.caption: Designer Daniel Olatunji keeps making clothes the slow, hard way.
body: The Nigeria-born, London-based Central Saint Martins graduate turned down outside investment early on.
'I'm really stubborn,' he says, even when it hurts the business.
The label is known for extreme handcraft.

items.headline: Japanese artisans remake old Polo Ralph Lauren
items.caption: Mended, patched and embroidered classics at the first PoloFest in Tokyo.
body: The Reimagined collection uses traditional Japanese mending on classic Polo pieces.
Highlights include chinos embroidered with smiley faces and patchwork ties.
How to wear it: one repaired piece with otherwise plain clothes.

items.headline: Hiroshi Fujiwara's wardrobe is his résumé
items.caption: How the 'godfather of streetwear' dresses, and why it matters.
body: Fujiwara brought hip-hop and skate culture to Tokyo in the 1980s.
He mentored Undercover's Jun Takahashi and worked with Loro Piana and Eric Clapton.
His look: simple, precise and endlessly copied.

items.headline: A day in Paris with model Jarrod Scott
items.caption: The Chanel Allure Homme Sport face shares his coffee, dinner and negroni spots.
body: The Melbourne-born model has walked Paris menswear runways since his early 20s.
His first coffee stop: Café Nuances.
He now splits time between Melbourne and the south of France, running a cocktail brand, Goldenbird.

items.headline: Yes, you can wear a gold watch every day
items.caption: GQ argues 18-karat shouldn't be saved for special occasions.
body: Wear it to lunch, parties and lazy days in the park, GQ says.
A gold watch dresses up a plain tee and jeans more than you'd think.
How to wear it: no other jewellery, let it be the one thing.

items.headline: Six baby river dolphins born in the Mekong
items.caption: Cambodia's endangered Irrawaddy dolphins grow to 118.
body: The calving season brought six calves to a 75-mile stretch of the Mekong in northeast Cambodia.
Local people see the dolphins as reincarnated ancestors, which has helped protect them.
Conservationists say it shows the species can recover if threats are curbed.

items.headline: A man named Service cleans up a dump himself
items.caption: Told to stop filming and clean it himself, Joshua Service did.
body: The Queens resident filmed piles of rubbish under a rail bridge in Crown Heights and called out the city.
Commenters told him to clean it himself, so he showed up with gloves and a rake.
He filled about 10 trash bags.

items.headline: Seabirds could help islands survive rising seas
items.caption: Reefs near seabird-rich atolls grew up to 2.5 times faster.
body: Lancaster University scientists studied 28 islands in the Pacific and Indian oceans.
Bird droppings fertilise reefs, which act as breakwaters and supply sand that builds islands.
Restoring seabirds and native plants could help some atolls keep pace with sea level rise.

items.headline: Shanghai's new opera house has a staircase for everyone
items.caption: Snøhetta's Grand Opera House opens with a spiral stair anyone can climb.
body: The building rises on the banks of the Huangpu River.
Its fan-inspired outdoor staircase leads to a public viewing platform, ticket or not.
The architects wanted to remove the barriers that keep people out of opera houses.
